Article Title: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow amid one-fifth cut to 2026 spending forecast
Article Text:
Tesla cuts 2026 capex by one fifth

SpaceX merger puts Tesla's spending under scrutiny

Revenue beats estimates, but net income plunges 43%

FSD adoption and automotive margins improve

Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent less than anticipated on capital expenditure.However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast has raised questions about its investment plans for artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and autonomous driving. The company now expects capital expenditure of around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not specify which areas would see lower spending.In the quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent a year earlier but well below the $7.5 billion analysts had expected on average, according to LSEG data.The lower spending helped Tesla report free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with market expectations of a cash outflow of $4.92 billion.Tesla's shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the results, supported by positive free cash flow, higher gross margins and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. However, the stock reversed direction to trade 2% lower. Shares have fallen around 14% this year."The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers exchange-traded funds tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon."The results come as chief executive Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX, his space venture. The unexpected cash generation could strengthen Tesla's financial position ahead of a possible deal, but lower investment in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots could raise concerns about its ability to deliver on its growth ambitions.On Tuesday, Musk described a merger between the two companies as a "good idea" and said they had formed special committees to discuss the proposal. He declined to provide further details during Wednesday's conference call with analysts.A combination would bring together businesses central to Musk's long-term vision of an integrated technology and manufacturing group spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.However, investors will want to see whether Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk's ambitions into commercial businesses, particularly as the robotaxi rollout has lagged behind his promises."The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com."The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter."Tesla's financial performance presented a mixed picture. Revenue remained flat compared with a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that had supported sales in the previous year. Nevertheless, the figure exceeded Wall Street's expectations.Net income fell 43% during the quarter.Tesla said it had ended the quarter with its largest backlog of passenger vehicles in four years. Higher petrol prices have supported demand for electric vehicles, particularly in Europe.The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, putting it on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years."Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."Tesla also reported stronger adoption of its driver-assistance technology in North America. The FSD (supervised) attach rate exceeded three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the second quarter, the company said.Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, reached 18.1% in the third quarter, above analysts' estimate of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.Tesla's energy business has recently helped offset pressures on its automotive operations. The latter remain under scrutiny as competitors worldwide launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla continues to rely heavily on its ageing Model 3 and Model Y.Despite the competitive pressures, Tesla aims to produce five million vehicles annually by around 2030, compared with an expected 2.5 million this year.
Article Summary: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow, beating Wall Street's expectations. Company cuts 2026 capex forecast by one fifth to $20 billion, down from $25 billion. Results come as CEO Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX.

Article Title: Rupee under pressure: Currency slips to 94.50 as oil rises, Dalal Street struggles in red
Article Text:
Rupee gives up some gains

NEW DELHI: Rupee weakened in early trade on Thursday, losing 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar as rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall.The currency opened at 94.47 at the interbank foreign exchange market before slipping to 94.50. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the dollar on Wednesday.Forex analysts said the rupee was trading on a flat-to-lower note amid pressure from the domestic stock market and higher oil prices. The dollar’s weakness and easing US Treasury yields offered some support to the currency.Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, expects rupee to retain a slight positive bias."We expect the rupee to trade with a slight positive bias on IPO related foreign inflows and weakness in the dollar. Softening of US treasury yields and reports that Russia is ready for new peace talks may also support the rupee," he told PTI.Choudhary added that market participants would track the weekly unemployment claims data from the US for further direction.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.21 per cent to 101.56. In contrast, Brent crude futures rose 1.58 per cent to $110.54 per barrel.Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak NEO, said the rupee remained finely balanced within the 94-97 range."The RBI has bought itself time, the Jio IPO has added near-term dollar supply, and a US trade agreement could strengthen the structural inflow story. But if portfolio selling accelerates again or crude makes a decisive move towards $120, that balance will be tested," Banerjee added.The domestic equity market also remained under pressure during early trade. BSE Sensex dropped 642.51 points to 73,067.18, while NSE Nifty50 declined 241.35 points to 22,570.90.Despite the weakness in equities on Thursday morning, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers in the previous session. They purchased equities worth Rs 1,022.32 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee loses 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday. Rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise against the dollar.

Article Title: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia raise concerns over oil supplies
Article Text:
Crude prices hold above $110 per barrel

Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of Hormuz

US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks rise

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.The threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.US crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy backed the proposed talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%. US state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region. Latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday.

Article Title: Wife’s father paid to buy house in couple’s joint names; Kerala High Court grants her exclusive ownership, rules husband must vacate after he fails to prove he paid anything
Article Text:
As the relationship between the couple deteriorated, the woman asserted that the house belonged solely to her. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the court rule in the wife's favour?

A property is in the joint name of a husband and wife. But only one of the two has directly or indirectly supplied funds for its purchase? In case of a marital discord, who can claim ownership of it?The Kerala High Court has declared a house registered in a husband and wife’s joint names to be the wife’s exclusive property after finding that her father had funded the entire purchase. The court directed the husband to vacate the property within three months.The dispute involved a couple who got married in 2012. The woman maintained that her father had financially supported the couple and bought a house in the names of both his daughter and son-in-law.After the wedding, the woman accompanied her husband abroad, where they lived for some time before eventually returning to India.As the relationship between the couple deteriorated, the woman sought the return of her gold ornaments and asserted that the house belonged solely to her because her father had financed its purchase.Also Read | Homebuyers paid Rs 2.06 crore but got no flat, builder said payments meant accepting delay; Bombay HC orders interest payout from 2017 saying RERA allows for unconditional right to monthly interest The married couple’s dispute was related to a seven-cent plot with a residential building in Manjeri, Malappuram district. The property was purchased in 2015, and registered in both their names.The woman told the court that her father had paid Rs 30 lakh to purchase the house for her future security. Although the property was registered jointly, she maintained that her husband had contributed nothing towards the purchase and therefore had no independent entitlement to half of it.The Malappuram Family Court examined the evidence and accepted that the woman’s father had funded the purchase. However, it did not grant her exclusive ownership. Instead, it directed her husband to pay her Rs 15 lakh, which is the value of his half share.The husband challenged the decision, maintaining that he had bought the property using his own money. The woman also appealed, seeking a declaration of her exclusive ownership and an order requiring him to vacate the house.Also Read | Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full relief The woman’s father testified that he had raised funds through a loan. His bank statement showed a credit of Rs 25 lakh followed by a debit of the same amount on November 9, the date of the sale deed.The husband maintained that he had used his own money to purchase the property. However, he failed to present evidence explaining where the funds for the sale consideration had come from.When questioned on this during cross-examination, the husband acknowledged that he had not withdrawn the money from any bank account. Instead, he claimed that his brother-in-law, who was working abroad with him, had given him the funds.But the court noted tht he did not examine his brother-in-law or produce documents. The court noted that he had failed to establish that he paid any part of the consideration.It concluded that “the entire sale consideration was paid by the father of the petitioner.”Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penalty The court also considered Section 45 of the Transfer of Property Act, which deals with the respective interests of people in property purchased using their separate funds. It found that the money had been provided by the woman’s father for her benefit and that the husband had not established a contribution of his own.It held that the appropriate relief was “declaring the exclusive ownership of the property upon the petitioner, while incidentally permitting her to obtain vacant possession thereof.”Asha Kiran Sharma, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the Kerala High Court focused on who had actually financed the purchase rather than relying solely on the names recorded on the property's title deed.In this case, the wife's father established that he had paid for the house using funds raised through a bank loan.Sharma explained that Section 45 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that, when two or more people jointly purchase a property and there is no agreement to the contrary, their respective shares are generally determined by the amounts they contributed towards the purchase.Since the husband had not contributed any money, his name on the deed did not establish an actual financial interest in the property. The Kerala High Court therefore recognised the wife as the sole owner and directed her husband to vacate the house within three months.In effect, the wife's claim succeeded because her father's bank records provided evidence of the source of the purchase money.Sharma said that when parents provide money towards a property, the arrangement should be documented clearly as either a gift or a loan. Where co-owners contribute different amounts, the ownership proportions should also be specified in the title deed or a separate written declaration. This can help avoid disputes that may arise when a property is registered jointly but the financial arrangement rests on an informal, undocumented understanding.Also Read | Tenant claimed landlords withheld Rs 10 lakh security deposit and refused to vacate shop; Delhi High Court rules against him, orders payout for unauthorised stay
Article Summary: The Kerala High Court has declared a house registered in a husband and wife’s joint names to be the wife's exclusive property. The dispute involved a couple who got married in 2012. The woman maintained that her father had financially supported the couple and bought a house in the names of both his daughter and son-in-law.

Article Title: HDFC Bank probes 2 executives for leak of sensitive information
Article Text:
HDFC Bank is currently investigating potential leaks of confidential information to social media and other outsiders.

The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way.

Info leak: HDFC execs may face regulatory action

MUMBAI: HDFC Bank is investigating whether two executives shared unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) with outsiders in violation of Sebi regulations and the bank’s code of conduct. UPSI can include data on financial results, dividends, capital raising and the appointment of key managerial personnel. The probe comes as the bank prepares for a leadership change, with incoming MD & CEO Anup Bagchi set to take charge on Oct 27, a day after Sashidhar Jagdishan steps down.The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way. “In line with our policies, a review is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts. To protect the integrity of the process and the privacy of all parties involved, we do not comment on active internal reviews,” the bank said.Employees can face regulatory action not only for sharing UPSI but also for trading in a company’s shares while in possession of such information. Sebi recently issued an administrative warning to Reliance Industries Ltd’ compliance officer after an investigation into trades between June and Aug 2024 found that two employees and an immediate relative had traded in the company’s shares while in possession of UPSI.The Securities Appellate Tribunal upheld Sebi’s insider trading penalties against a former employee of Nucleus Software who had shared advance information about the company’s “huge profits” with a relative.Bloomberg first reported the investigation into the alleged leaks. According to the report, the executives oversee key businesses and functions at HDFC Bank. The bank identified them during an internal investigation launched after some senior leaders grew concerned about possible information leaks, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. The probe is continuing as the bank examines whether the information was misused, according to the report.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank is investigating whether two executives shared unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) with outsiders. UPSI can include data on financial results, dividends, capital raising and the appointment of key managerial personnel. The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way.

Article Title: SBI confirms data leak, says 4,000 customer records identified on dark web
Article Text:
The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.

Independent assessment is under way: SBI

MUMBAI: SBI has confirmed a data breach involving 3,897 customer records containing personal information, which were found on the dark web.SBI identified the records containing personal information in a preliminary analysis of 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web.The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on Oct 16.The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 3,75,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.In its notice to stock exchanges, SBI said the preliminary analysis had identified records containing customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records.The leak of PII can lead to impersonation, loan and benefit frauds and existing account takeovers.The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. It has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In, India’s national cyber incident response agency, to conduct an independent assessment. SBI said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally. It said the assessment was underway and remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.
Article Summary: SBI identified the records containing personal information in a preliminary analysis of 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web. The leak of PII can lead to impersonation, loan and benefit frauds and existing account takeovers. The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.

Article Title: Carmakers look to Diwali to rev up sales
Article Text:
FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri. (File photo)

FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri

CHENNAI: India’s carmakers are counting on Dhanteras and Diwali to sustain festive sales momentum, even as dealers’ body FADA reported a sharp year-on-year decline in passenger vehicle (PV) registrations during Navratri. The decline, however, needs to be seen against the high base created by the GST rate cuts in Sept 2025, which lowered vehicle prices and unleashed a surge in demand during the festive season.Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles — among the country’s top players, together accounting for two-thirds of PV sales — have reported strong bookings and deliveries during Navratri, raising hopes that demand will hold up through Diwali.However, FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri to 1,82,728 units from 2,34,004 units in 2025. Last year, buyers had deferred purchases ahead of the GST rate cuts that took effect on Sept 22, driving pent-up demand and inflating the base for this year’s comparison.Maruti Suzuki said retail sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra rose 35% year-on-year, with small-car sales increasing around 16% and SUV sales doubling.Its retail sales during Navratri were almost on a par with last year. “The festive season has been encouraging for Maruti Suzuki, with strong customer demand through Navratri,” said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing and sales of the company.Maruti began Oct with pending bookings of around 2 lakh units, which increased to 2.7 lakh after Dussehra. “We expect double-digit growth over the overall festive period through Diwali,” Banerjee said.Hyundai Motor India has also reported healthy demand, supported by sales during Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi. Registrations up to Navratri festival rose about 30% year-on-year to nearly 41,000 units.“Considering the pace of bookings, we expect momentum to continue through Dhanteras and Diwali. Demand remains healthy across both urban and rural markets,” said Tarun Garg, MD & CEO of the company.
Article Summary: FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri. The decline, however, needs to be seen against the high base created by the GST rate cuts in Sept 2025. Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles — together accounting for two-thirds of PV sales — have reported strong bookings and deliveries.

Article Title: RBI rejects all 224 bids in treasury-bill auctions
Article Text:
File photo

MUMBAI: For the first time since March 2025, RBI on Wednesday rejected all the 224 bids in the three treasury-bill (T-bill) auctions through which govt was set to borrow Rs 23,000 crore.Due to a tight fund-flow situation in the system, on the back of a high govt balance, GST-related outflows and funds getting blocked primarily in the Jio Platforms IPO, bidders wanted higher rates in the auction, bond market players said.On the other hand, RBI was reluctant to pay high rates because this could have indicated elevated rate signalling for the short term by the central bank. What helped RBI’s cause was the high cash balance with govt which was at about Rs 5.3 lakh crore. With govt flush with cash and not in immediate need of funds, RBI could afford to reject all bids in the T-bill auction, a bond dealer said. This decision by the central bank gels well with its policy narrative of ‘calibrated tightening’.In Wednesday’s auction, RBI had received 77 bids for 91-day T-bills worth Rs 8,000 crore, 68 bids for 182-day T-bills and 79 bids for 364-day T-bills.
Article Summary: For the first time since March 2025, RBI rejected all the 224 bids in the three treasury-bill (T-bill) auctions through which govt was set to borrow Rs 23,000 crore. On the back of a high govt balance, GST-related outflows and funds getting blocked primarily in the Jio Platforms IPO, bidders wanted higher rates.

Article Title: Rate hike: RBI more hawkish than external members at meet
Article Text:
File photo

MUMBAI: The Oct Monetary Policy Committee minutes show that the governor and RBI members were more hawkish than the two external members, who favoured retaining the ‘neutral’ stance rather than shifting to ‘calibrated tightening’, arguing that inflation was driven predominantly by supply-side factors.RBI’s MPC voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, but split 4-2 on shifting to calibrated tightening, signalling rate cuts were off the table in the near term as inflation threatens to spread beyond food and fuel. Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governor Poonam Gupta, executive director Indranil Bhattacharyya and external member Saugata Bhattacharya backed the shift. External members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh favoured retaining the neutral stance, citing supply-driven inflation and growth risks.Calibrated tightening signals that “rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving circumstances and the outlook,” Malhotra said. The duration and extent of any rate-hiking cycle would depend on underlying inflation, the spread of price pressures, second-round effects of supply shocks and demand conditions.“While inflation is driven largely by supply-side factors and does not show any signs of overheating of the economy nor of generalisation, it is important to manage inflationary expectations,” Kumar said. He favoured a 25-basis-point rate hike but said a neutral stance remained appropriate amid geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties.Singh warned that shifting to calibrated tightening could signal an extended rate-hiking cycle and undermine the benefits of recent growth-supportive monetary and fiscal policies.
Article Summary: RBI’s MPC voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%. But split 4-2 on shifting to calibrated tightening, signalling rate cuts were off the table in the near term. External members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh favoured retaining the neutral stance.

Article Title: Security flaw: eMudhra shares take a hit, fall 20%
Article Text:
eMudhra certificates blocked by Google and Mozilla

Shares fell 20% on BSE.

BANGLURU/ NEW DELHI: Bengaluru-based digital trust and cybersecurity company eMudhra has acknowledged a cryptographic flaw that generated weak private keys linked to eight intermediate digital certificates in its global website-certificate business, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites. Shares fell 20% on BSE.The company said the affected TLS business accounts for around 1% of its revenue.eMudhra reported FY26 revenue of about Rs 710 crore and EBITDA of roughly Rs 110 crore. It had guided for revenue growth of 15–18%, with greater emphasis on higher-margin enterprise solutions.The flaw occurred during a key-generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, when a second set of weak keys was generated alongside the original strong keys. Mozilla cryptography engineer Dennis Jackson reported the issue on Oct 17, flagging insufficient randomness that made the keys vulnerable to recovery. eMudhra said it was investigating the root cause.eMudhra said it was working with affected customers to replace Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates and prevent disruption. Co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told TOI that no certificates had been issued from the affected root in India and that only one US customer had received certificates under the affected infrastructure.The company said its infrastructure had not been breached and its Indian digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign and enterprise solutions businesses remained unaffected.Govt officials said the ministry of electronics and IT has taken serious note of the incident with a special team constituted to investigate the matter.“The impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval… Important to note that Digital Signature Certificates and eSign services regulated by Controller of Certifying Authorities, remain completely unaffected by this incident,” an official said.Mozilla blocked six affected certificates, released Firefox security updates and removed the relevant root certificate from its trust store. Google blocked the affected public keys, extending protection to supported Android devices, while Cloudflare introduced safeguards. Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) warned that compromised keys could enable website impersonation, interception of communications and the issuance of fraudulent code-signing certificates that make malicious software appear legitimate. It advised organisations to install the latest security patches.
Article Summary: eMudhra acknowledged a cryptographic flaw that generated weak private keys linked to eight intermediate digital certificates in its global website- certificate business. The flaw occurred during a key-generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, when a second set of weak keys was generated alongside the original strong keys. Shares fell 20% on BSE.

Article Title: At 7.9%, core sector clocks fastest growth in new series
Article Text:
Representative photo

Core sector grew 7.9% in Sept, compared with 3.1% a year ago, driven by strong performance in electricity, cement and refinery products and aided by a favourable base as well, official data released Tuesday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 5.9% in Aug. This is the strongest performance of the core sector in the new series with the revised base year.Output in the energy-dominant industries like natural gas (-4.6%), crude oil (-1.4%) and fertilisers (-11.7%) saw continued sequential contraction, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia. Output in the refinery products (10.3%) and coal (10.7%), however, saw acceleration during the month.Output in the infrastructure-dominant industries such as electricity (11.4%) and steel (4.9%) showed positive growth in Sept. In the newly added iron ore industry, output further accelerated (18.4%) during the month.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said Sept figures highlight buoyancy in infrastructure where govt has been spending.
Article Summary: Core sector grew 7.9% in Sept, compared with 3.1% a year ago. Strong performance in electricity, cement and refinery products. Growth marked acceleration from an upwardly revised figure of 5.9%. This is strongest performance of the core sector in the new series with the revised base year.

Article Title: Surge in gold loans partly reflects stress, say lenders
Article Text:
Representative image

The trend raises questions about whether gold-backed lending is driven by consumption or income-generating needs or is merely helping borrowers manage debt by shifting loans.

MUMBAI: A surge in gold loans may partly reflect borrower stress, with lenders allowing customers already in deep delinquency to borrow against gold and repay overdue loans, Macquarie said in a report. The trend raises questions about whether gold-backed lending is driven by consumption or income-generating needs or is merely helping borrowers manage debt by shifting loans.During the company’s Q2FY27 earnings, Piramal Finance MD & CEO Jairam Sridharan said 15% to 23% of gross gold loan disbursements across the industry over the past year went to customers already more than 90 days overdue. Piramal’s policy bars lending to such borrowers.In its earnings call last week, Bajaj Finance said it was moving away from short-tenor gold loans, which can trigger accidental delinquencies when customers fail to repay the full principal and interest on time. The company prefers longer tenors that offer borrowers greater flexibility.“Auction is not liked by any constituent... so it’s better to manage it through risk rather than manage it through auction is how we have taken a position to be,” a company official said.According to RBI data, gold loans accounted for a third of incremental retail lending in Q1FY27. Suresh Ganapathy, an analyst at Macquarie, said gold had become the second-largest retail loan book after mortgages, accounting for 28% of non-housing retail loans.Citing Piramal’s comments on borrower stress, he said collections teams at other banks and NBFCs could be directing overdue borrowers to pledge gold and borrow from another lender to clear existing NPAs.He also cautioned that many lenders were rushing into the business without fully recognising the accompanying risks.
Article Summary: The trend raises questions about whether gold-backed lending is driven by consumption or is merely helping borrowers manage debt by shifting loans. 15% to 23% of gross gold loan disbursements across the industry over the past year went to customers already more than 90 days overdue.

Article Title: HDFC Bank probe finds executives leaked confidential information: Report
Article Text:
HDFC Bank probe finds two senior executives shared sensitive information with outsiders

HDFC Bank faces scrutiny as leadership transition approaches

NEW DELHI: HDFC Bank has found evidence that two senior executives shared confidential business plans and possibly market-sensitive information with outsiders, according to a Bloomberg report.The probe began after some bank leaders raised concerns about possible leaks. The two executives, who oversee key businesses and functions, were identified during the investigation. The bank is still checking whether the information was misused.The findings were shared with senior management, including some board members, earlier this year. Both executives have been formally informed of the findings, but it is not yet clear what action the bank will take. The sources spoke on condition of anonymity as the matter is confidential.An HDFC Bank spokesperson confirmed that an internal review was underway but declined to comment on the findings or the executives involved.“In line with our policies, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts,” the spokesperson said via email to Bloomberg. “Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete.”The bank said it was committed to high standards of ethics and governance and took reports of possible violations seriously.The investigation comes as HDFC Bank prepares for a change at the top following a period marked by boardroom disputes and senior management departures. The lender, valued at about $115 billion, is India's largest bank by market value and has spent three decades building a reputation for conservative management, strong internal controls and consistent profitability, Bloomberg reported.Its share price has declined about 28% this year.Anup Bagchi, a veteran of rival ICICI Group, is scheduled to become the bank's chief executive later this month, on October 27. His appointment will make him the first outsider to take up the position. The transition follows the unexpected decision by incumbent chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan not to seek another term. Jagdishan is stepping down after six years leading the bank.Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director and one of HDFC Bank's longest-serving executives, has also asked to leave at the end of December.The findings of the internal probe add to the challenges facing the lender as it prepares for the leadership change.The latest developments follow a series of internal disagreements that have surfaced publicly in recent months.In March, then-chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences between his personal values and certain practices at the bank. HDFC Bank subsequently commissioned an independent legal review, which said Chakraborty's concerns were not substantiated.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank has found evidence that two senior executives shared confidential business plans and possibly market-sensitive information with outsiders. The bank is still checking whether the information was misused. Both executives have been formally informed of the findings, but it is not yet clear what action the bank will take.

Article Title: Delhi AQI jumps from 179 to 244 in a day; GRAP-1 restrictions kick in across NCR
Article Text:
Delhi's air quality deteriorated to the 'poor' category, triggering Stage 1 measures under the Graded Response Action Plan

What restrictions come under GRAP-1?

How are the GRAP stages triggered?

What other anti-pollution measures has Delhi announced?





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘poor’ category on Wednesday, prompting the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage 1 measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the National Capital Region (NCR) with immediate effect.Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI), which stood at 179 in the ‘moderate’ category on October 20, rose to 244 by 2pm on October 21, according to the CAQM order, news agency PTI reported.The sub-committee on GRAP took the decision after reviewing the prevailing air quality, meteorological forecasts and pollution levels.Forecasts by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) indicated that Delhi’s AQI was likely to remain in the ‘poor’ category over the coming days.Under Stage 1 of GRAP, the use of coal and firewood as fuel in tandoors at hotels, restaurants and open eateries is prohibited.The use of diesel generator sets is restricted, with exemptions for emergency and essential services as specified under the plan, PTI reported.The CAQM has directed agencies concerned across the NCR to implement the measures immediately and ensure that air quality does not deteriorate further.It has also urged citizens to follow the restrictions and cooperate with enforcement agencies.GRAP is a set of emergency measures implemented in stages to prevent further deterioration in air quality. The restrictions become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise.Stage 1 is invoked when the AQI is in the ‘poor’ category, between 201 and 300.Stage 2 applies to the ‘very poor’ category, with AQI between 301 and 400.Stage 3 is triggered when the AQI is between 401 and 450, while Stage 4 applies when it exceeds 450.The GRAP-1 action comes days after the Delhi government announced its winter action plan to tackle air pollution.The plan, scheduled to run from November 1 to February 28, includes a ban on the entry of vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI emission standards.The government has also announced a ‘No PUC, No Fuel’ policy, under which vehicles without a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate will not be allowed to buy fuel at petrol pumps.Other measures include restrictions on construction and demolition activities, checks on the transportation of construction materials and steps to control road dust.The government has also proposed measures to promote public transport and electric buses as part of its broader effort to curb pollution during the winter months.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI), which stood at 179 in the ‘moderate’ category on October 20, rose to 244 by 2pm on October 21. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage 1 measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the National Capital Region (NCR) with immediate effect.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Chennai, schools shut in 4 districts
Article Text:
Heavy rain affected Chennai and nearby areas, prompting school closures as a precautionary measure.

The Regional Meteorological Centre reported significant rainfall across the city and adjoining districts.





CHENNAI: Heavy rain lashed Chennai and neighbouring districts overnight, prompting authorities to declare a holiday for schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu on Wednesday.Chennai collector S Malathi Helen and the collectors of the three neighbouring districts ordered the closures as a precautionary measure amid forecasts of further heavy showers.According to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), weather stations at Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. Several parts of the city, including Taramani, Villivakkam and Nandanam, also received moderate to heavy showers.A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. The wet spell is expected to continue until Oct 26, while another low-pressure area may form over the Bay of Bengal around Oct 23.Meanwhile, the early-morning holiday announcement caught some government school kitchens off guard.Staff had begun preparing breakfast for students in Classes 1 to 8 under the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme before the closure order was issued.“The holiday was declared only around 6am. We started preparing breakfast around 5.30am. We are looking to distribute it to conservancy workers,” a headmaster said.District authorities said any decision on Thursday's closure would depend on the intensity of rainfall and a review of weather conditions on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu closed as a precautionary measure. Weather stations recorded more than 10cm of rainfall as of 6am on Wednesday. A low-pressure area is likely to develop over the southwest Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Tamil Nadu coast.

Article Title: Russia to send first diesel shipment to US on Thursday amid global supply crunch
Article Text: Russia will send its first 40,000-tonne diesel shipment to the United States on Thursday, under an agreement with President Donald Trump to resume Russian fuel supplies, Russia's deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said.The move comes as global diesel markets face a supply squeeze, while Ukraine has warned that renewed Russian energy exports could help finance Moscow's war effort.According to Reuters, Novak said further shipments would follow the agreement between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Trump, adding that Moscow would meet US demand within its capabilities. The first cargo is part of a broader supply plan announced by President Trump.Trump has announced plans for Russia to supply 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel initially, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes thereafter. The arrangement is aimed at increasing fuel supplies amid a global diesel shortage and rising prices.Russia had imposed a ban on diesel exports after Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries disrupted production and caused fuel shortages in the country.On October 9, Moscow lifted the ban, allowing Russian suppliers to resume diesel shipments to international markets.The development comes after US President Donald Trump pushed for a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine targeting attacks on energy infrastructure. The proposed arrangement aimed to halt strikes on oil refineries, power facilities and other energy sites, as attacks on critical infrastructure disrupted fuel supplies and added pressure on energy markets.Ukraine has opposed easing restrictions on Russian energy exports, arguing that additional revenue from diesel sales could help Moscow finance its war effort.President Volodymyr Zelensky criticised the US-Russia arrangement, warning that allowing Russia to expand fuel exports while the war continues could weaken pressure on the Kremlin to end the conflict.Europe is also facing growing pressure on diesel supplies as disruptions to Middle Eastern exports tighten the market. Reuters reported in September that the disruption had cut Europe's diesel and jet fuel supplies by about a quarter, pushing fuel inventories to a 12-year low.Nigeria's Dangote refinery has increased exports to Europe to help fill the gap, highlighting the region's growing reliance on alternative suppliers.Reuters reported on October 21 that analysts expect the US-Russia diesel deal to have limited impact on global fuel prices, as the promised supplies may be too small to ease the market shortage. Analysts also questioned whether Russia could meet the announced export targets given damage to its refineries and rising shipping costs.With EU restrictions limiting direct imports of Russian fuel, the additional supplies are unlikely to provide an immediate solution to Europe's diesel concerns.
Article Summary: Russia will send its first 40,000-tonne diesel shipment to the United States on Thursday. The move comes as global diesel markets face a supply squeeze. Russia had imposed a ban on diesel exports after Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries disrupted production and caused fuel shortages.

Article Title: Playing doubles with AI: How human judgement becomes the winning partner
Article Text:
Industry leaders at Elevate Connect London emphasized the need for human judgement in AI adoption and implementation

‘AI should complement human capabilities’

Business context and governance key to scaling AI

How much Data Quality is enough for AI?

Polar explorer draws parallels with business leadership

LONDON: As businesses accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), industry leaders have stressed the importance of human judgement, trusted data and strong governance in turning technological capabilities into meaningful business outcomes.The issue was central to Elevate Connect London 2026, the flagship event organised by Mumbai-based IT multinational ADROSONIC for senior leaders in the UK insurance market. Held at the Four Seasons Hotel London at Tower Bridge, the invitation-only gathering focused on the theme “AI Predicts. Humans Decide.”Discussions covered AI adoption, data quality, business transformation and leadership, with speakers emphasising that technology alone cannot deliver value without human expertise and organisational readiness.One of the key sessions was a fireside conversation titled “Playing Doubles with AI”, featuring Mayank, founder and CEO of ADROSONIC, and Hasani Jess, group CTO of Aventum Group.Drawing on the example of tennis legend Leander Paes, Mayank compared effective human-AI collaboration to a doubles partnership, where complementary strengths matter more than identical capabilities.“Great doubles partnerships are not built by finding someone identical to you,” Mayank said.“They are built by combining complementary strengths and compensating for one another’s weaknesses.”He cited Paes’s career to illustrate how ambition, context and human judgement can defy expectations based solely on data. While AI can process information, conduct research and improve efficiency, people must interpret that information and decide how to act on it.Jess said effective AI use requires practice and expertise, despite the technology’s apparent accessibility.“AI is intoxicatingly familiar,” he said. “It looks easy because we can all interact with it. But just as watching a professional athlete is very different from performing at that level, working effectively with AI requires discipline, learning and experience.”The speakers also discussed the importance of trust, noting that confidence in AI systems must develop through repeated use and demonstrated reliability. With models evolving rapidly, organisations must continually reassess how best to combine human and machine capabilities.For Mayank, the real opportunity lies in using AI to achieve outcomes that would otherwise be beyond an organisation’s reach.“If AI is only helping us do the same things faster, that is one plus one equals two,” he said. “The real opportunity comes when AI enables us to do things we could not do before. That is when one plus one becomes eleven.”Another panel examined how businesses can expand AI adoption while protecting human expertise, governance and client trust.James Welch, head of delivery at Miller, said AI deployment must reflect the risks associated with individual business functions.While high-risk areas such as claims and payments require strong human oversight, tasks such as generating renewal packs could benefit significantly from automation. He added that protecting the company’s brand, expertise and client relationships remained a priority.Nitin Agrawal, lead business architect at ADROSONIC, said adoption, rather than technology, was often the biggest challenge.He stressed the need to redesign operating models, upskill employees and involve business users in developing AI initiatives.Daniel Del Moro, director of AI and automation innovation at UiPath, highlighted the importance of reliable data and well-defined processes.He cautioned against treating AI as a cure-all, arguing that businesses must first address process inefficiencies and data-quality problems. Combining established technologies such as robotic process automation (RPA) with newer AI tools could help unlock greater value, he said.The panel’s broader message was that AI adoption should be treated as a business transformation programme, supported by leadership, change management, clear accountability and end-to-end objectives, rather than as an isolated technology project.Data readiness was another focus, with leaders from AUB Group, Hampden Risk Partners, Oneglobal Broking and ADROSONIC discussing how businesses can establish reliable data foundations without delaying AI projects in pursuit of perfect information.The panel agreed that data should be trustworthy, understood and fit for the decision it is intended to support.Raj Rai said competitive advantage would depend not merely on adopting AI, but on understanding data quality, lineage, governance and how the technology is applied within an organisation.Ben Ormerod noted that the level of data quality required depends on the decision being made. Although AI can accelerate business outcomes, poor-quality inputs can also speed up poor decisions. He also highlighted AI’s potential to identify data-quality issues and trace data lineage.Marc Steel said AI should support rather than replace human expertise, particularly in relationship-driven sectors such as specialty insurance, where client relationships and market context remain important.Kamlesh Yadav cautioned that confidence expressed by AI systems should not be mistaken for accuracy. He emphasised the need for trusted information, clear ownership, human oversight and measurable business outcomes.The discussion highlighted the need to balance experimentation with safeguards, ensuring that innovation does not come at the expense of security, accountability or sound decision-making.The event also featured a keynote by polar explorer Ann Daniels, who drew on her expeditions across the Arctic and Antarctica to discuss leadership, resilience and decision-making under uncertainty.Daniels described operating in environments where conditions can change without warning, resources are limited and decisions can have serious consequences. In such situations, success depends on preparation, teamwork and the ability to adapt when plans no longer work.Her experiences offered parallels with the challenges facing businesses as AI capabilities, market expectations and competitive pressures evolve. Just as polar explorers must reassess conditions and adjust their routes, business leaders must make decisions without always having complete information.Daniels emphasised that technology and data can support decisions, but leaders still need to judge when and how to act on the information available. Her keynote reinforced the event’s broader focus on adaptability, collaboration and human judgement during periods of change.A Boardroom Live session also examined a proposal to expand ADROSONIC’s Digital Innovation Lab at BIT Mesra.Across the sessions, speakers returned to a common theme: AI’s value depends not only on what the technology can do, but also on the quality of the data, processes and decisions surrounding it.As organisations move beyond experimentation, effective adoption will require combining technological capability with human expertise, clear governance and trust.
Article Summary: Industry leaders emphasise the need for human judgement in AI adoption and implementation. The issue was central to Elevate Connect London 2026, the flagship event organised by Mumbai-based IT multinational ADROSONIC. Discussions covered AI adoption, data quality, business transformation and leadership.

Article Title: 'Can't compromise data': Malaysia bans civil servants from using Waze, citing links to Israel
Article Text:
Malaysia has barred civil servants from using Waze over data security concerns linked to its Israeli origins

Malaysia has banned civil servants from using Alphabet-owned navigation app Waze, citing concerns over data security linked to the app's Israeli origins, following a review ordered by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.The prohibition took effect immediately, according to a letter dated Tuesday from chief secretary to the overnment Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to heads of government agencies.Anwar said the government was examining potential security risks associated with Waze, which he said “was bound to Israeli laws”.“We cannot compromise on the security of people's data and identities,” news agency Reuters quoted Anwar saying in a Facebook post after chairing a meeting of the national cybersecurity committee on Tuesday.The prime minister did not specify the security risks identified but recommended that government employees use TuJu, a domestic mapping application developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative.Waze, founded in Israel, provides real-time traffic updates using satellite signals and data crowdsourced from drivers. Google parent Alphabet acquired the app in 2013 for about $1 billion.The decision comes against the backdrop of Malaysia's strong support for the Palestinian cause. The Muslim-majority country does not maintain diplomatic relations with Israel.
Article Summary: Malaysia bans civil servants from using Google-owned navigation app Waze. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim cites concerns over data security linked to app's Israeli origins. Waze provides real-time traffic updates using satellite signals and data crowdsourced from drivers.

Article Title: SpaceX profits skyrocket to $4.4 billion as revenue jumps 161%, AI business surges 830%
Article Text:
SpaceX revenue surges 161% to $14.6 billion in Q3

Starlink adds 1.6 million subscribers in three months

Computing capacity expands as investment climbs

SpaceX's Super Intelligence business has become the biggest driver of the company's latest quarterly growth, helping Elon Musk's aerospace company report a net profit of $4.4 billion in the July-September quarter.Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, rising 161 per cent to $14.6 billion, while spending on infrastructure also increased sharply.The company's third-quarter results showed a turnaround from the year-ago period, when SpaceX recorded a net loss of $1.1 billion on revenue of $5.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA, which measures operating performance, rose 306 per cent to $8.8 billion from $2.2 billion.The Super Intelligence (SI) business, covering computing infrastructure, models and software applications, generated $7.6 billion in revenue during the quarter. This was an 830 per cent increase from $813 million in the corresponding period last year.SpaceX said the segment added $6.7 billion in year-on-year revenue through its solutions and infrastructure. Growth was attributed to new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and wider adoption of Grok products by enterprise customers and consumers.Connectivity services, led by Starlink, remained another major source of revenue for SpaceX.The segment brought in $5.2 billion in the quarter, marking a 69 per cent increase from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Its operating income rose 99 per cent to $2.4 billion.Starlink's consumer subscriber base reached 13.6 million as of September 30, compared with 7.2 million a year earlier. It added 1.6 million subscribers during the quarter. Monthly average revenue per user rose to $69 from $66 in the previous quarter.Space-related activities contributed $1.8 billion in revenue, up 6 per cent year-on-year. SpaceX completed 12 customer launches during the July-September period.The company also reported that its first orbital Starship flight delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The deployment added around 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.SpaceX's expansion came with a steep rise in capital spending. Capital expenditure stood at $19.6 billion in the third quarter, against $6.9 billion in the same period last year, largely due to investment in computing infrastructure.The company's computing capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts by September 30, compared with 0.6 gigawatts a year earlier, as it continued building infrastructure for its Super Intelligence business.The chief financial officer said the company intended to pursue expansion while keeping its investments and balance sheet on a disciplined footing."We are building the infrastructure of the future with discipline--focused on capital efficiency, strong returns on invested capital, and maintaining a robust, investment-grade balance sheet--while moving with the velocity to capture the opportunity in front of us," the CFO said.
Article Summary: SpaceX revenue surges 161% to $14.6 billion in Q3. Starlink adds 1.6 million subscribers in three months. Super Intelligence business adds $6.7 billion in year-on-year revenue. SpaceX completed 12 customer launches during the July- September period.

Article Title: AI boom set to push Big Tech investment beyond $1 trillion in 2027, says UBS
Article Text:
Tech giants' AI spending to exceed $1 trillion in 2027

AI spending supports US economic growth

Rising investment puts pressure on cash flows

Big tech firms are set to splurge over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027 as demand for computing power continues to grow faster than supply, according to a report by UBS.The investment boom is also helping boost US economic growth, even as companies face rising funding needs. Spending on AI infrastructure is expected to cross $600 billion in 2026 before topping $1 trillion in 2027, the report stated.“Demand has exceeded capacity ahead of schedule,” UBS said, pointing to the growing pressure on companies to expand their computing infrastructure to keep up with demand.It expects spending to rise further over the next year, although the pace of growth could peak in 2027. Higher investment is putting pressure on companies’ cash flows and increasing their need for additional funding.The growing investment in AI infrastructure has become a significant contributor to the US economy. According to UBS, spending on AI infrastructure added around 0.75 percentage points to US gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first half of 2026.Rising equity prices linked to AI companies have also boosted household wealth and consumption, providing another source of support for economic activity.However, the report found little clear evidence that AI has so far led to a substantial increase in overall productivity or widespread job displacement.Its estimated effect on the overall unemployment rate remains limited, at around 0.2 percentage points or less.The impact on employment has varied across industries. Selected high-technology sectors, including software and computer systems design, recorded a 1.4 per cent year-on-year decline in employment. In contrast, construction industries supporting data centre infrastructure saw employment grow by nearly 3 per cent.While demand for AI infrastructure continues to drive investment, UBS has flagged emerging financing pressures among major technology companies. Their cash flows have weakened as spending has increased, while demand for their bond issuances has become less robust.The report said investors expect free cash flow to return to positive territory in 2028, provided companies are able to generate sufficient revenue from AI services.The ability to convert heavy infrastructure spending into sustainable revenue will therefore remain important as the investment cycle progresses.AI demand is also contributing to higher prices in some areas, including software, digital goods and electricity, according to UBS. However, the report noted that productivity gains from AI could help reduce inflation over time.The outlook for the investment cycle will depend on whether demand for computing power continues to exceed available capacity and whether technology companies can turn their growing investments into sustainable revenue growth.
Article Summary: Spending on AI infrastructure is expected to cross $600 billion in 2026 before topping $1 trillion in 2027. Higher investment is putting pressure on companies’ cash flows and increasing their need for additional funding. Growing investment in AI infrastructure has become a significant contributor to US economy.

Article Title: 24 million barrels a day: Gulf oil flows surge past prewar levels despite US-Iran war
Article Text:
Oil flows from the Middle East have topped prewar levels at over 24 million barrels a day despite escalating attacks on shipping in Hormuz

How oil is moving despite the attacks

Attacks raise the cost of shipping

Iran's leverage over oil flows weakens

Persian Gulf oil exports have climbed above prewar levels despite intensifying attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as tankers adapt to the risks with US protection and alternative routes help keep supplies moving.Oil flows from the Middle East, including shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, averaged more than 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, exceeding the prewar average of 23.3 million barrels a day, according to ship-tracking firm Kpler.However, shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remain below their earlier levels. Preliminary estimates put average flows through the strait, including offshore transfers in the Gulf of Oman, at around 14 million barrels a day during the same period, about 82% of prewar volumes, the Wall Stree Journal reported.The recovery comes as the risks to shipping remain high. Around 30 attacks on vessels have been reported in October, accounting for about 20% of all ship attacks recorded during the war, according to Michelle Wiese Bockmann, a senior analyst at maritime intelligence firm Windward.An improvised shipping system, supported by US protection, has helped tankers continue carrying crude through the high-risk waterway.Some vessels make short trips into the Gulf to load oil before travelling through Hormuz and transferring their cargo to other ships near Oman for onward delivery.Tankers often switch off their tracking signals during parts of these journeys. American air cover provides some protection along a corridor near the Omani coast, although vessels remain vulnerable to attacks.Pipelines running across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also helping exporters bypass the strait. Around 40% of non-Iranian crude shipped out of the Gulf in September travelled through routes that avoided Hormuz, compared with 17% before the war, Kpler estimated.“The big picture is that the system for shipping through a dangerous Strait of Hormuz is now well-established and the risk appetite of those involved in exporting oil has risen,” said Hamad Hussain, a senior commodities economist at Capital Economics.The increased willingness to take risks is partly driven by the potential returns. Traders can earn around $20 more per barrel by reselling Iraqi oil than before the war, according to Homayoun Falakshahi, Kpler's head of crude oil analysis. That translates into an additional $40 million on a supertanker carrying a typical cargo of two million barrels.Shipowners are also offering higher payments to attract crews willing to make the dangerous crossings. One China-based ship-staffing company offered seafarers as much as $25,000 for a round trip that typically takes one or two weeks, The Wall Street Journal reported.“The volumes remain high despite rising attacks, because profits make it worth the risk,” Falakshahi said.The continued movement of oil has not made the route safe. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has used drones and missiles against vessels attempting the crossing, while small boats have also been used to target shipping.The risks were illustrated by the Tanzania-flagged supertanker "Loyalty", which entered the Persian Gulf twice in September and October to load Iraqi crude. After transferring two million barrels of oil to another tanker in the Gulf of Oman in early October, it returned to the Gulf for another cargo.On October 16, the vessel was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat, maritime security company Vanguard said. The projectile damaged a freshwater tank while the tanker was carrying two million barrels of Iraqi crude, according to a crew member.The danger has pushed up the cost of transporting oil. Freight for a supertanker carrying Gulf crude to China approached a record $37.37 per barrel this week, Kpler said. War-risk insurance premiums have risen to as much as 10% of a vessel's value, from less than 3% before the conflict, according to Windward.“In April, the problem was a shortage of crude. In October, it is the cost of moving it,” said Natasha Kaneva, head of the global commodities strategy team at JPMorgan.Brent crude rose to around $108 a barrel on Tuesday, reflecting concerns that the improvement in oil flows may not last if fighting intensifies again. With global inventories thinning, any renewed disruption could leave markets with limited room to absorb a supply shock.The recovery in regional exports contrasts with the pressure on Iran's own oil trade, which has been constrained by a US maritime blockade.Tehran has sought to reassert control over Hormuz, warning that neighbouring countries should not be able to export oil if Iran cannot ship its own. But the continued movement of crude through the strait and alternative routes has weakened its ability to deter regional shipments.“Iran would have to be more aggressive to achieve the same degree of control it previously possessed over oil flows from the region,” Hussain said.That leaves the market facing two competing realities: oil exports have recovered beyond prewar levels, but the cost and danger of moving crude remain elevated. Whether the recovery can be sustained will depend on the security of shipping routes and whether the conflict escalates further.
Article Summary: Oil flows from the Middle East averaged more than 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18. Around 30 attacks on vessels have been reported in October, accounting for about 20% of all ship attacks recorded during the war. An improvised shipping system, supported by US protection, has helped tankers carry crude through the high-risk waterway.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude tops $110 as Middle East tensions threaten shipments
Article Text:
Oil prices climb over 1% (representative image)

Tanker attacks raise concerns over oil supplies

Oil prices retreat from five-month high

US works to increase fuel supplies

Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed concerns over Middle East supplies amid growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $1.18, or 1.21 per cent, to $99 per barrel.The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief during a meeting in Tehran.Supply concerns intensified after a supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy.Iranian media reported that the vessel had been “violating” Iranian regulations.At least 18 vessel attacks were reported over a two-week period, ship-tracking firm Kpler said in a note on Monday.The attacks have also spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.“Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz,” LSEG analysts said in a note.“Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on,” the analysts added.The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and the airports in Riyadh and Abha, Saudi Arabia.Meanwhile, the death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified, Reuters reported.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Tehran had not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.Despite Wednesday's gains, crude prices had fallen in the previous session after reaching elevated levels.Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at $108.79 per barrel on Tuesday, after touching a five-month high of $111.99.The November contract for US WTI crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled $1.87 lower, down 1.8 per cent, at $101.79 per barrel.In the United States, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday that they were working with refiners around the world to increase fuel production as a diesel shortage pushed prices higher.US crude oil inventories were also expected to have declined in the week ended October 16, alongside stocks of refined petroleum products, according to an extended Reuters poll.The eight analysts surveyed by Reuters estimated that US crude inventories fell by an average of around 800,000 barrels during the week.Market participants are monitoring developments across the Middle East, including threats to shipping routes and energy infrastructure, for their potential impact on oil supplies and prices.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 1.21 per cent to $99 per barrel. The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief.
